cards.text: Paul, an apostle writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), just said nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ (Romans 8:39). Now his voice drops. He says, "I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit."

cards.question: True or false: Paul says his heart is full of joy.

cards.text: Paul says he has deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in his heart. For the sake of his brothers, his own flesh and blood, he could wish that he himself were cursed and cut off from Christ.

cards.question: Paul says the covenants, the giving of the law and the temple worship belong to his brothers. They are the people of ___.

cards.text: And there's more that's theirs: the adoption as sons, the divine glory, the promises and the patriarchs. Friend, that's not a list, that's a whole TROPHY CASE.

cards.question: Paul says Someone comes from Israel by human descent, and he calls Him God over all, forever worthy of praise. Who is He?
Paul says, "It is not as though God’s word has failed." What reason does he give?

answers.text: Not all descended from Israel are Israel
All of Israel kept the law perfectly
The promises were never for Israel

cards.text: Paul goes on: being descendants of Abraham, Israel's forefather, doesn't make them all his children. Abraham had a son named Ishmael by Hagar, and a son named Isaac, the one God promised Sarah would bear (Genesis 16:15; 17:19).

cards.question: Paul quotes a Scripture that says Abraham's offspring will be reckoned through ___.
True or false: Paul says it's the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.

cards.text: Paul quotes the promise itself from Genesis 18:14: "At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son." Then he turns to Rebecca, Isaac's wife, whose children came from one man, Isaac himself. Same dough, same batch, same oven.

Those children were twins, and before they were born or had done anything good or bad, Rebecca was told something about them. They'd done NOTHING yet, friend, and I spent years in the back of a junk drawer doing NOTHING, so I know it when I see it.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says God's plan of election stands by works.

cards.text: And here's what Rebecca was told: "The older will serve the younger." The older twin was Esau, and Jacob was born right after him (Genesis 25:25-26).

cards.question: Paul quotes Malachi 1:2-3 about these twins. Which one does it say God loved?

cards.text: The whole line goes, "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated." That's a heavy one, friend.
Paul doesn't wait for the group chat to blow up. He asks it himself: "What then shall we say? Is God unjust?"

cards.question: How does Paul answer his own question, "Is God unjust?"

cards.text: To back that up, Paul goes to something God said to Moses, Israel's leader.

cards.question: What does God tell Moses about His mercy?

answers.text: He'll have mercy on whom He has mercy
He'll have mercy on all who keep the law
He'll have mercy on Israel's priests only

cards.question: True or false: Paul says God's mercy depends on how hard a person tries.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to Pharaoh, king of Egypt in Moses' day, who watched plague after plague hit his land (Exodus 7-12). Paul quotes Exodus 9:16, where the Scripture tells Pharaoh the purpose God raised him up for.

cards.question: The Scripture says to Pharaoh that God raised him up so He might display His ___ in him.
True or false: The Scripture says to Pharaoh that God wants His name proclaimed only in Egypt.

cards.text: Paul sums it up: God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden. Then Paul says one of his readers is going to push back.

cards.question: What does Paul expect one of his readers to ask him?

answers.text: Why God chose Israel at all

cards.text: The full question goes, "Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?" Paul answers, "But who are you, O man, to talk back to God?"

cards.question: True or false: Paul pictures something that was formed asking its maker, "Why did You make me like this?"

cards.text: Friend, I've got a mustache where my hands should be, and you don't hear ME asking why. Then Paul paints a picture: a potter at work with one lump of clay.

cards.question: From that same lump of clay, what does Paul say the potter has the right to make?

answers.text: A special vessel and a common one

cards.text: Paul keeps going with a what-if. What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?

cards.question: In Paul's what-if, God bears with the vessels of His wrath with great ___.

cards.text: And what if He did it to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, prepared in advance for glory? GREAT patience, friend, and I'm a stamper who opens the oven door every two minutes to check.

cards.question: Paul says the vessels of mercy include us, the ones God has called. Who has He called them from?

answers.text: Both the Jews and the Gentiles

cards.text: Paul backs that up by quoting Hosea, a prophet in Israel (Hosea 1:1, 10; 2:23).

cards.question: In Hosea, God says He will call some people ‘My People.’ Who are they?

answers.text: Those who are not His people
Those who already were His people

cards.text: Then Paul quotes Hosea again: "It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’"

Then Paul quotes Isaiah 10:22-23, and Isaiah, another prophet (Isaiah 1:1), CRIES OUT concerning Israel. Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, could ring out like that, and the whole kitchen would stop and listen.

cards.question: Isaiah says that though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, who will be saved?
True or false: Isaiah says the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth slowly and only halfway.

cards.text: Paul adds one more line from Isaiah 1:9, just as Isaiah foretold. It's about the descendants the Lord of Hosts left, and what would have happened without them.

cards.question: Isaiah says that unless the Lord of Hosts had left them descendants, they would have become like which cities?
